title: Resting potential as a systems-level causal factor rather than specific channels

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Resting potential as a systems-level causal factor rather than specific channels

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because tumor suppression was obtained with either chloride- or potassium-based hyperpolarization, the authors argue that a systems-level physiological property — resting membrane potential — rather than any specific ion channel acting as an oncogene or tumor suppressor, can be a powerful causal factor regulating tumorigenesis.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, in complement to the gene-focused idea of specific ion channels being intrinsic oncogenes or tumor suppressors [44, 48, 145], we suggest that a systems-level physiological property – resting potential – can be a powerful causal factor in regulating these processes.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem”. Scope: Bioelectric control of tumorigenesis generally, argued from Xenopus laevis oncogene experiments

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The use of potassium- and chloride-based interventions partially separates voltage from a specific channel. Coverage is too narrow and voltage matching too incomplete to establish resting potential as the general causal variable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare tumor suppression across several channels and ion species after matching achieved Vmem, and test whether Vmem predicts incidence better than channel identity. Divergent effects at matched voltage would refute the systems-level formulation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ion-specific off-target effects remain.

Matched quantitative Vmem values across treatments are limited.

Only a small set of channels and ionic manipulations is represented.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.8

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Suppression by two different ionic routes is published and is the right kind of evidence for a voltage-level rather than a channel-identity cause. The summaries are not a voltage-matched series, and raw voltages are not public. The Xenopus contrasts therefore speak to part of the general causal claim and leave the matched test incomplete.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Match the degree of hyperpolarization achieved by a potassium channel and by chloride loading, and test whether tumor suppression follows voltage rather than channel identity. Equal suppression at equal voltage, and loss of suppression when voltage is clamped back, would support the systems-level claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The two treatments were not published as voltage-matched dose responses.

Chloride loading and potassium-channel expression can share non-voltage effects.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.74
analysis feasibility: 0.5
data existence: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.42
